title: Alternative Data Pipeline
oneLiner: serverless pipeline syncing 175,000+ job postings a day from 6 ATS platforms across 61% of the S&P 500 into Postgres and an S3/Athena lake — for under $15 a month
cardDescription: infrastructure-as-code job-posting pipeline: 6 ATS adapters, SQS self-continuation past the Lambda 15-minute ceiling, and Lambda timeouts driven from ~37 per cycle to zero
overview: an alternative-data pipeline for equity research: it tracks hiring as a signal by scraping job postings from the applicant-tracking systems that big companies actually run on. everything is infrastructure-as-code under AWS SAM, and the whole thing runs for less than a streaming subscription. the interesting engineering is not the scraping, it is surviving Lambda's 15-minute wall without dropping work.
whatIBuilt: per-ATS adapters (Ashby, Lever, Phenom, SmartRecruiters, SuccessFactors, Oracle Cloud) behind one shared runner
an SQS self-continuation loop so a worker that runs out of clock commits what it has and re-enqueues itself
EventBridge scheduling, CloudWatch alarms on source degradation, and Alembic-managed Postgres schema
an S3/Athena lake for the historical snapshots the Postgres tables do not keep
howItWorks: a dispatcher fans companies out to per-ATS scrape jobs on SQS
each worker runs against a time budget, fetching 16 pages concurrently
when the budget runs out it commits progress and re-enqueues its own cursor, so nothing is lost at the 15-minute ceiling
rows land in Postgres for querying and in S3 for Athena over the history

title: AI Chief of Staff
oneLiner: event-driven core of a 7-engineer multi-agent system that scores delivery risk across concurrent consulting engagements from 32 GitHub, Slack, Linear and Notion webhook types
cardDescription: multi-agent project monitoring — per-project Redis locks and timestamp-scored queues keep each project's events ordered while projects analyse concurrently
overview: consulting engagements go wrong quietly — a stalled Linear board, a channel that went silent, a PR nobody reviewed. this ingests all of it from Notion, Slack, Linear and GitHub and turns it into a prioritised risk briefing. i owned the event-driven core underneath it.
whatIBuilt: the ingest worker, the part every webhook passes through before any agent sees it
the concurrency model, which was the hard part: ordering has to hold inside a project without serialising across projects
retry backoff and dead-letter handling, so a follow-up fetch that fails is retried and then parked rather than lost
howItWorks: FastAPI validates the HMAC signature, extracts metadata, enqueues and returns 200 immediately
webhook payloads are sparse, so a worker fetches the actual content from each platform's API
each project gets its own Redis lock and a queue scored by event timestamp
agents score the signals and the dashboard surfaces prioritised risk

title: seanpatrickmay.github.io
oneLiner: this site. four live data feeds, four years of Garmin plotted on a map, and every page drawn as paper — all of it static HTML on GitHub Pages with no backend
cardDescription: my portfolio — live Garmin, Spotify, Goodreads and Duolingo feeds, hand-drawn project covers, and two maps built from four years of activity data
overview: A static-exported Next.js site that still feels current, because scheduled workflows write fresh JSON into the repo rather than a server answering at request time. The look is a scrapbook: kraft board, pinned paper, rubber-stamped headings, and project covers drawn as index cards in SVG so they cost nothing and follow dark mode.
whatIBuilt: a static Next.js export with a home page, a project wall, and a page per project, all driven from one projects.json
scheduled GitHub Actions that refresh Garmin, Spotify, Goodreads and Duolingo into committed JSON, with a data-loss guard so a failed fetch never blanks a card
two maps from the same projection code: an aged nautical chart with flags for work and study, and plotting paper with weighted dots for everywhere I've run, ridden or skied
a Lighthouse CI gate that fails the build on accessibility, SEO or best-practices regressions, and warns rather than fails on performance because runner load is noisy
howItWorks: scheduled workflows fetch each feed and commit JSON into public/
a one-off local script pages the full Garmin history, resolves each place from its own GPS, and writes only a coarse per-place centroid
pages import that JSON at build time, so every route is static HTML
GitHub Pages serves the built output

annotation tooling and notebooks for training and evaluation
flask inference server and browser-facing prediction flow

title: Wildfire Modeling
oneLiner: ConvGRU-U-Net that predicts where a wildfire spreads over the next hour. F1 0.929 on four held-out California fires, from 38 channels fused out of GOES, VIIRS, MODIS, fire weather and terrain
cardDescription: wildfire spread prediction — a ConvGRU-U-Net with CBAM attention on a 38-channel satellite fusion, at F1 0.929 against a 0.832 logistic-regression baseline
overview: Six generations of model for one question: given where a fire is now, where will it be in an hour? The final system is FireSpreadNet, a ConvGRU-U-Net with CBAM attention over a 38-channel stack of satellite, weather and terrain data, trained on eight California fires.
whatIBuilt: a data pipeline that pulls GOES fire detections through Earth Engine, masks cloud with DQF, and fuses VIIRS and MODIS, GRIDMET weather and 3DEP terrain into training arrays
FireSpreadNet: a ConvGRU-U-Net with CBAM attention that predicts a whole next-frame fire image from a sequence, trained with focal + Tversky loss
an XGBoost per-pixel classifier and a logistic-regression baseline, so the neural network has to justify itself against something simpler
a 6-stage ablation harness that adds one feature group at a time and keeps only what moves F2
a React and FastAPI viewer that plays a fire back hour by hour against the model's prediction
howItWorks: Earth Engine exports GOES fire detections for a fire's bounding box, hour by hour
a 7-stage label pipeline cleans the raw detections — majority-vote smoothing over 5 frames is what turned a noisy signal into a learnable one
prev_fire_state[t] is defined as labels[t-1], which removes temporal leakage by construction rather than by remembering to shift a column
the ConvGRU-U-Net consumes a 6-frame sequence and predicts the next frame in full
nextSteps: generalise past California — every fire in the training set shares a fuel and terrain regime
calibrate the probabilities, so the output can drive a decision rather than a picture

coverArt.line: predicts the next hour of a fire

leadFigure.caption: creek fire, hour 186: last hour, what happened, what the model said

metrics.label: F2, recall-weighted, on four fires the model never saw
F1, equal-weight, against 0.884 for XGBoost on the same features
F1 gained from fixing the labels and features, with the model unchanged

findings: fire state alone carries most of XGBoost's feature importance: spread is strongly autocorrelated, so any honest model has to beat that prior
F2 rather than F1 as the target, because missing a fire costs more than a false alarm

title: PokerML
oneLiner: CFR+ solver for heads-up no limit — k-means card abstraction, 100K iterations of external sampling, and a web UI where you can play the bot and see its ranges live
cardDescription: poker solver with 100K iterations of CFR+, card bucketing, and a web app with live 13x13 range heatmaps
overview: this is a heads-up no-limit hold'em solver built on CFR+ and external sampling monte carlo. it trains over a card and bet-size abstraction, then serves the converged strategy through a fastapi web app where you can play against the bot and see its 13x13 range grid in real time.
whatIBuilt: CFR+ trainer with external sampling MCCFR, immutable game states, and per-iteration bucket caching for speed

card abstraction: heads-up, all 169 preflop hands keep a bucket of their own; flop and turn hands are clustered by earth mover's distance over where their strength can go, and river hands by OCHS, strength against clusters of opponent hands
action abstraction with 75%, 100% and 175% pot preflop, up to five geometric sizes postflop from a small blocking bet to an overbet, fold/check/call, all-in, and a 4-raise-per-street cap
fastapi server with session management, bot inference, and a 13x13 range grid API for the frontend
nextSteps: expand action abstraction with more bet sizings and raise depths

title: RepoWiki
oneLiner: Generates a feature-scoped, citation-backed wiki for a git repository, and keeps it current as the code changes
cardDescription: a wiki for any git repo, organised by feature, where every claim cites the code lines it rests on
overview: RepoWiki reads a repository's source and git history, clusters its files into features, and writes a Wikipedia-style article for each one. Every claim on a page cites the code lines or commits it rests on. When new commits make a claim stale, it finds that claim and rewrites the page around it. It built every wiki linked from this site.
whatIBuilt: an indexer that reads a repository at a given revision and clusters its files into features
the writing pipeline that calls the Claude API for structured, cited sections
staleness detection that maps changed lines back to the claims that cite them
an Astro site generator with search, history pages and a JSON export
an evaluation framework that measures how well the wiki describes the repository

title: AlphaSettler
oneLiner: A Settlers of Catan engine in Rust, searched with information-set Monte Carlo tree search, about 300× faster per step than Catanatron
cardDescription: Catan in Rust: a full-rules engine, tree search over hidden hands, and Python bindings
overview: AlphaSettler simulates Settlers of Catan in Rust with every rule enforced, then searches it with information-set Monte Carlo tree search. Catan hides information, from opponents' hands to the development-card deck, so each decision samples worlds consistent with what the bot has actually seen and searches across them. A seat-rotating arena over common random numbers compares bots without seat luck, and PyO3 bindings expose the engine to Python.
whatIBuilt: a Rust Catan engine with full rule enforcement and every legal move encoded as an integer from 0 to 664
ISMCTS with belief-state sampling, PUCT selection and batched leaf evaluation
a bot arena with seat rotation, common random numbers and multi-threaded matches
PyO3 bindings and a CLI for matches, statistical comparisons and self-play
an adapter to Catanatron 3.3, so both engines can be tested against each other
a learned evaluator: a value/policy network, trained by self-play, that replaces the hand-set heuristic as the bot's evaluator

leadFigure.caption: random players on one M1 Pro; catan-rl runs its own trade menu

metrics.label: faster per engine step than Catanatron, in the same random-play benchmark
tree-search simulations a second, on one core
win rate over 800 games against three Catanatron alpha-beta bots (even share: 0.25)

findings: a flat strength curve against a weak bot is the opponent's ceiling, not the search's: against itself, the learned-evaluator bot keeps gaining from more simulations

title: RotoText
oneLiner: Text that reshapes itself to where your eyes are, so it reads face-on from any angle, using webcam eye tracking
cardDescription: webcam eye tracking and geometric projection, so text reads face-on from wherever you are
overview: RotoText finds your face and irises in the webcam feed with MediaPipe, estimates where your eyes are in 3D from the iris size and midpoint, and projects the scene onto the screen from that point. Move your head and the text moves with you, as if it were behind the glass. It runs on desktop and phone cameras and drives a Line of Sight puzzle game built on the same projection.
whatIBuilt: eye tracking on MediaPipe face and iris landmarks
geometric projection from 3D eye position to the screen
scene rendering for the 3D box and its targets
a Line of Sight puzzle game on top of the projection
device presets for desktop and phone cameras
